# The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

## *Pelochelys cantorii*

---

![Asian Giant Softshell Turtle](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/Pelochelys_cantorii.jpg/640px-Pelochelys_cantorii.jpg)
*Asian Giant Softshell Turtle - Pelochelys cantorii*

---

## Introduction

The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*) is one of the largest freshwater turtles in the world. Named after Danish zoologist Theodore Edward Cantor, this remarkable reptile can grow up to six feet in length and weigh over 220 pounds (100 kilograms). Despite its impressive size, this turtle remained largely mysterious to scientists for many decades.

## Habitat and Behavior

This species inhabits slow-moving freshwater rivers, streams, and estuaries across Southeast and South Asia, including countries such as India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Philippines. The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle spends approximately 95% of its life motionless beneath the sand or mud at the bottom of rivers. It surfaces only twice daily — primarily to breathe. Rather than actively hunting prey, it ambushes fish, crustaceans, and mollusks that swim nearby.

## Physical Characteristics

Unlike hard-shelled turtles, this species possesses a flat, olive-colored, leathery carapace instead of a rigid shell. Its head is relatively small compared to its massive body, featuring a long, fleshy, pig-like snout that functions as a snorkel, allowing it to breathe while remaining mostly submerged.

---

![Softshell Turtle Habitat River](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Mekong_River.jpg/640px-Mekong_River.jpg)
*Freshwater river habitat typical of the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle*

---

## Conservation Status

The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle is listed as **Endangered** on the IUCN Red List. Major threats include overhunting for meat and traditional medicine, egg collection, and habitat destruction caused by dam construction and river pollution. In 2007, a significant discovery in Cambodia revealed a surviving population of approximately 150 individuals, offering renewed hope for conservation efforts.

## Conservation Efforts

Several wildlife organizations and local governments are working to protect nesting sites and educate local communities. Conservationists monitor nesting beaches and implement egg protection programs to help increase population numbers.

---

## Bibliography

Asian Turtle Trade Working Group. *Pelochelys cantorii*. IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, 2000, www.iucnredlist.org/species/16502/97397263. Accessed 15 Oct. 2023.

Hogan, C. Michael. "Asian Giant Softshell Turtle." *Encyclopedia of Earth*, edited by C. Cleveland, National Council for Science and the Environment, 2011, www.eoearth.org.

Turtle Conservation Coalition. *Turtles in Trouble: The World's 25+ Most Endangered Tortoises and Freshwater Turtles*. IUCN/SSC Tortoise and Freshwater Turtle Specialist Group, 2018, pp. 34–36.
